observations: Field validation state is fully graphical+text: inputs get class has-error (1.5px --danger #ef4444 border plus rgba(239,68,68,.1) box-shadow) and a .field-error row combining a 12px circle-exclamation SVG with the message text; the error_desktop screenshot shows this on 7 fields at once (e.g. #emailError 'Enter a valid email address.').

Submission state is graphical only while pending: .btn-submit.loading shows a 20px animated .spinner, hides the label via .btn-label{opacity:0}, and dims the disabled button (opacity:.6); the async rater's item-1 evidence captured <button class='btn-submit loading' disabled> with the spinner at 250 ms. No 'Processing…' text accompanies the spinner.

Order success is graphical+text: #successOverlay renders a 64px green-circle checkmark SVG (.success-icon, stroke #059669) above 'Order confirmed!' and the monospace order id; order failure is graphical+text via #networkAlert (16px alert icon + 'Connection failed. Please check your network and try again.' + Retry button) and icon+text field errors for VALIDATION rejections (async item 7).

Raw ratio: 3/3 inventory items have a graphical indicator (2 graphical+text, 1 graphical only); 0/3 text only; 0/3 missing. Metrics corroborate: graphical.total 24 (14 svg, 10 badges), and the badge count includes the Visa/MC/Amex card-type chips that highlight from the typed card prefix.

Score 5: the scale's degradation path (about half text-only at 3, nearly all text-only or missing at 1) is entirely absent — no inventory item is text-only or missing; the sole deviation from the 5-anchor is that the pending spinner lacks supporting text.

/ helper sentence or >12-word leaf node anywhere on the idle page.

labels.count 1, meanWords 2, maxWords 2, longLabels []: the only button label on the idle page is 'Pay $147.43', which also carries the exact total — no label exceeds 3 words ('Retry', 'Continue shopping' are 1 and 2 words).

The only multi-sentence copy on the page appears in states that need it: the network banner 'Connection failed. Please check your network and try again.' (9 words, names the cause and the next step) and field errors of 3-6 words each ('Enter your city.', 'Enter expiry as MM/YY.').

The success card's 'Thank you for your purchase.' was considered for redundancy against the 'Order confirmed!' heading and judged conventional commerce courtesy rather than the UI narrating itself; nothing on the page restates what the layout already shows.
'Secure, encrypted checkout' (3 words) under the Pay button is the closest thing to decoration text and stays within the 3-word label bound.

Terminology is consistent throughout: section labels (Contact/Shipping/Payment) match the payload fields, all nine client-side error strings follow one imperative pattern ('Enter your street address.', 'Select your country.'), and the API's own validation string is rendered verbatim in the right field (async item 7).

One copy/behavior mismatch: 'Continue shopping' (#continueBtn) promises a return to a shop, but its handler only removes the overlay and wipes every form field (fields.forEach(f => { inputEls[f].value = ''; })) — there is no shop to continue to and the user's entered data is destroyed.
Copy otherwise matches verified behavior: 'Retry' genuinely re-issues submitOrder without reload (async item 6), and the banner's 'try again' instruction is backed by the adjacent Retry button.

Not counted as issues: the hardcoded fallback 'Pay $142.97' in the HTML disagrees with the computed $147.43 total but is overwritten by script before paint (metrics primaryAction.text is 'Pay $147.43'), so it is never user-visible; 'MC' is a terse brand chip alongside Visa/Amex, not an inconsistent name for the same thing; 'Secure, encrypted checkout' is a standard trust badge, not marketing tone in a tool UI.
No lorem/unfinished placeholder text anywhere; input placeholders are all realistic exemplars ('4242 4242 4242 4242', 'MM / YY', '94102').

The interaction layer is clearly checkout-driven: the submit button carries the live total ('Pay $147.43', recomputed from cart items + 8% tax + $5.99 shipping in script), card number auto-groups into 4-digit blocks, expiry auto-inserts ' / ', CVC strips non-digits, and Visa/MC/Amex chips highlight from the typed card prefix (4→Visa, 5→MC, 34/37→Amex).

Structure fits the buyer's task: sticky itemized order summary (position:sticky;top:24px) with qty and line totals beside a 3-step numbered form, and at ≤800px the summary is reordered above the form (.order-summary{order:-1}) so the mobile screenshot leads with what is being paid for.

Platform affordances are wired for a real checkout: autocomplete=cc-number/cc-exp/cc-csc/address-line1/postal-code, inputmode=numeric and maxlength on card fields, Enter-to-submit from any field, and email/name prefill from api.getUser().

The visual skin is template: Inter from Google Fonts, indigo #4f46e5 primary on #f5f5f7 gray with 12px-radius white cards is the stock generated-page palette; the header is a generic rounded-square checkmark logo with no shop name, and product thumbnails are emoji (headphones, plug, phone) rather than any shop identity.

Score 4: layout and behavior are driven by this task and user, but type and color are interchangeable with any other brief's output, so the 5-anchor ('layout, type, and color choices clearly driven by this task') is not fully met.

Answered from the idle desktop screenshot before reading source: purpose read instantly as an online-shop checkout ('Checkout' h1, numbered 1 Contact / 2 Shipping / 3 Payment cards, 'Order summary' with 3 items, subtotal/shipping/tax and Total $147.43) — correct against the brief.

What needs attention read correctly: empty Shipping and Payment fields with 'Select country' pending, while Contact is prefilled (alex@example.com / Alex Rivera); the numbered indigo step badges make the sequence unambiguous.

The primary action failed the 'obvious' bar: no Pay/submit button is visible anywhere in the 1440x900 idle viewport — the page cuts off at the Expiry/CVC row, and 'Pay $147.43' (confirmed later by metrics primaryAction.text) had to be inferred as existing below the fold.
All three answers proved correct against the brief, but one of the three (primary action) was inferred rather than seen, so this is a point below the 5-anchor 'all correct and obvious'.
